contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tostig Godwinson was Harold Godwinson’s brother, former earl of Northumbria, and ally of Harald Hardrada in the 1066 invasion of England.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Tostig Godwinson was born c. 1026, associated with England. The early evidence is uneven, so precise details should be treated carefully.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Tostig Godwinson is remembered as the embittered brother whose grievance helped bring on the crises of 1066, and the sources present a proud and increasingly desperate figure consumed by rivalry with his brother Harold Godwinson. As earl of Northumbria he provoked a revolt by his harsh rule, and when Harold failed to restore him, Tostig turned against his own family, allying with foreign enemies of England.

That alliance led him to join Harald Hardrada's invasion, and he died alongside the Norwegian king at the Battle of Stamford Bridge — killed in a cause aimed squarely at his brother's throne. The sources, English in origin, present his career as a study in wounded pride curdling into treachery, though they also acknowledge the real grievance of his loss of office.

His personality survives as a portrait of resentment and ambition: a man who would rather see England invaded than accept his own fall. He is remembered as the brother whose bitterness opened a door to disaster, a figure of dynastic tragedy whose defection sharpened the chaos of the year of three battles.

contentSections.title: As earl and exile
paragraphs: Tostig’s rule in Northumbria provoked opposition and exile. His alliance with Harald Hardrada turned family conflict into part of the wider English succession crisis.
Battle of Stamford Bridge gives Tostig Godwinson's career a specific military and political setting: his choices, command, defeat, or death affected the outcome remembered in that article.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Killed with Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge in 1066 after joining the Norwegian invasion of England.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Tostig is remembered as one of the destabilizing figures of 1066, linking internal English politics to Norwegian intervention.

keyAchievements.title: Served as earl of Northumbria
keyAchievements.description: Tostig’s troubled rule in Northumbria ended in rebellion and exile, making him a dangerous enemy of his brother Harold.

keyAchievements.title: Allied with Harald Hardrada
keyAchievements.description: His alliance with Harald Hardrada gave the Norwegian invasion an English political dimension.

keyAchievements.title: Fought at Stamford Bridge
keyAchievements.description: Tostig died at Stamford Bridge, where the northern invasion collapsed before the Norman threat arrived.
